title: EF1 and Pareto optimality for additive mixed items
area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
formal: Does every finite instance of indivisible mixed-item allocation with \(n\ge3\) agents and arbitrary real additive utilities admit a complete allocation that is both envy-free up to one item (EF1) and Pareto optimal (PO)? The item removed to eliminate an agent’s envy may come from the envied bundle or from the envious agent’s own bundle, with at most one item removed in total.
why: Fairness and efficiency can conflict when an indivisible item benefits one participant and burdens another. This question asks whether one standard minimal relaxation of envy is always compatible with the absence of a Pareto improvement. Resolving it would determine whether a central fairness–efficiency guarantee survives unrestricted mixed valuations beyond the now-understood pure-goods and pure-chores existence settings.
status_note: The January 2026 Barman–Verma revision explicitly leaves standard EF1 together with PO open for unrestricted additive mixed manna. The checked September 2026 weighted-fairness results and November 2025 pure-chores theorem do not settle this target. The search through 2026-09-15 was bounded and does not certify that no later resolution exists.

progress.text: The survey’s Open Question 2 asks whether EF1 and PO allocations always exist for additive mixed items and at least three agents.
Mahara’s revised preprint states general additive-chores existence in Theorems 1.1–1.2, including the stronger fractional Pareto requirement. These theorems concern the pure-chores subcase.
Barman and Verma’s v3 establishes introspective EF1 with PO for mixed manna while explicitly identifying standard EF1 with PO as open.
Teh’s v2 gives weighted EF1 existence for arbitrary mixed additive values and separate efficiency results under restricted magnitudes; the checked results do not close the general joint guarantee.

importance.reason: EF1 and Pareto optimality for mixed goods and chores tests the compatibility of two fundamental allocation requirements.
importance.basis: Saved question, title, and category scope; importance review only, not a fresh proof or open-status review.

sentences: Each participant may value an indivisible item positively, negatively or at zero.
Every item must be assigned, and the participants have additive utilities and equal entitlements.
EF1 permits eliminating each envy comparison by removing at most one item from one of the two bundles.
The question is whether an allocation with this fairness guarantee can always also be Pareto optimal for at least three agents.
Recent results settle pure chores and some alternative mixed-item fairness guarantees, but the checked 2026 sources do not resolve the unrestricted combination.

definitions: The agents are \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and the items are \([m]\) for any integer \(m\ge0\). Each agent \(i\) has values \(v_{i,g}\in\mathbb R\), with no restrictions on their signs or magnitudes, and \(u_i(S)=\sum_{g\in S}v_{i,g}\) for every \(S\subseteq[m]\). The same item may have positive, zero or negative value to different agents. Agents have equal entitlements; no normalization of utility totals is imposed. An allocation \(A=(A_1,\ldots,A_n)\) is a partition of all items into pairwise disjoint bundles, which may be empty. Every item must be assigned exactly once. No disposal, monetary transfers or fractional assignment is permitted. Allocation \(A\) is EF1 if for every ordered pair of distinct agents \(i,j\), at least one of the following holds: \(u_i(A_i)\ge u_i(A_j)\); there exists \(g\in A_j\) such that \(u_i(A_i)\ge u_i(A_j\setminus\{g\})\); or there exists \(g\in A_i\) such that \(u_i(A_i\setminus\{g\})\ge u_i(A_j)\). These alternatives remove at most one item from one of the two bundles for this comparison only; they do not change the allocation. In particular, removing one item from each bundle is not allowed. Allocation \(A\) is PO if no other complete integral allocation \(B\) satisfies \(u_i(B_i)\ge u_i(A_i)\) for every \(i\) and \(u_j(B_j)>u_j(A_j)\) for at least one \(j\). The quantifiers are \(\forall n\ge3\;\forall m\ge0\;\forall v\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\;\exists A\), with both properties required of the same \(A\). The target is existence; there is no polynomial-time computation or representation requirement for an allocation-selection rule.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof of the universal existence statement, or a complete Lean-checked refutation. A refutation may specify a finite real-valued instance and prove that none of its complete integral allocations satisfies both defined properties. An existence theorem confined to pure goods, pure chores, two agents, restricted value magnitudes or a different envy relaxation does not prove the general statement. A computation-time bound is not additionally required.

context_blocks.text: Open Question 2 of the August 2024 survey asks for existence of an EF1 and PO allocation for at least three agents with additive utilities. Its subsequent question about polynomial-time computation is a separate issue. This card selects the stated existence question and uses the survey’s mixed-item EF1 convention.

The survey defines mixed-item EF1 by allowing deletion of at most one item either from the envied bundle or from the envious agent’s own bundle. All utility comparisons use the envious agent’s valuation. For purely nonnegative values the useful deletion is from the other bundle; for purely nonpositive values it is from the agent’s own bundle.

Mahara’s November 2025 revision establishes EF1 together with PO, and also fractional PO, for arbitrary additive chores. Consequently, the survey’s 2024 observation that even the chores case was unresolved is no longer an appropriate current-status description.

Barman and Verma’s January 2026 revision explicitly retains the general mixed-manna EF1-and-PO question. It proves PO together with introspective EF1, a different condition that modifies an agent’s own bundle. That result does not assert standard mixed-item EF1 together with PO.

Teh’s September 2026 revision establishes complete weighted EF1 existence for unrestricted additive mixed manna. Its joint fractional-efficiency guarantee applies to restricted value magnitudes, so the results checked there do not establish the unrestricted EF1-and-PO statement.
